raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Depends on #6259, #6303 (which contains #6293), #8017, #8043 and #8049. Please review the diff from the merge of their heads: [scoped diff](https://github.com/Connor-XY/Megatron-LM/compare/e6899429b1...yx/pstate-c5-optimizer-fallbacks). The base takes #8017's update that merges #6259 and sets the Gloo fields of `build_test_pg_collection`. #6303 is in the base because the test-caller commit uses `ProcessGroupCollection` in `tests/unit_tests/dist_checkpointing/utils.py` and `tests/unit_tests/training/test_param_norm.py`, which import it only with #6303. The base's process-group allowlist records the 172 reads of its tree, without the `T5Model` shim read that #6303 removes.

Land this after #8738. With Gloo groups on, the default, `setup_model_and_optimizer` passes no collection to `get_megatron_optimizer`. Without #8738, stock training would warn once there, and so would `test_training.py`, `test_fp8_param.py`, `test_fp4_param.py` and `test_cuda_graphs.py`.

**Why.** Three optimizer paths read the global `parallel_state` groups without a warning when the caller omits them:
- `get_megatron_optimizer` without `pg_collection` builds one with `use_mpu_process_groups()`;
- `clip_qk` without `dp_cp_group` reduces the attention logits over the global DP×CP group;
- `Float16OptimizerWithFloat16Params.sharded_state_dict` rebuilds the checkpoint entry of a GTP-remat shard that has no model entry, such as the Mamba and GDP `in_proj` weights under distributed Muon. The rebuild read the global TP and DP groups, even for an optimizer built from a collection.

A model on its own grid, such as a MIMO module, then sharded its optimizer state, clipped its weights or described its shards with another model's ranks. Without a global grid, the rebuild hit an assertion.

**What.**
- `get_megatron_optimizer` and `clip_qk` fall back through `resolve_process_groups`. It warns once with a `ProcessGroupFallbackWarning` (deprecated in 0.21, removed in 0.23) and returns the same groups as before:
  - `get_megatron_optimizer` builds every collection field, as `use_mpu_process_groups()` did. Several of the optimizers' readers treat an unset field differently from one set to `None`.
  - `clip_qk` resolves `dp_cp_gtp_remat`, and only when a layer has logits to reduce.
- `Float16OptimizerWithFloat16Params` takes a keyword-only `pg_collection`, which `get_megatron_optimizer` and `LayerWiseDistributedOptimizer` pass. The GTP rebuild takes `tp` from it, plus `dp_cp_gtp_remat` or, when that is unset, `dp_cp`, as the model's own entries do. A collection without `tp`, or with neither DP×CP group, raises `ValueError`. Without a collection, the rebuild warns and uses the global groups. It still resolves groups only when a shard needs a rebuild.
- 46 unit-test calls to `get_megatron_optimizer` and `get_megatron_muon_optimizer` pass `ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups()`. That is the collection the fallback builds, so these tests run on the same groups without the warning. Two of these calls are in main's new `test_shortcut_moe_training_and_clipping`, which the sync merge adapts so that it does not hit the warned fallback. The initializer-cleanup tests pass an empty collection instead of stubbing `use_mpu_process_groups()`.
- The checker goes from 172 reads to 171. The three fallbacks become guarded reads, and the rebuild reads one collection instead of two accessors.

**Tests.**
- New `tests/unit_tests/optimizer/test_optimizer_process_groups.py`:
  - the factory builds on the collection it is given, with global reads forbidden and the warning made an error;
  - the layer-wise optimizer hands its collection to the optimizers it wraps;
  - without a collection, the factory warns and builds the same collection as `use_mpu_process_groups()`;
  - the GTP rebuild uses the collection's groups for four field combinations and rejects a collection without a DP×CP group;
  - the rebuild warns without a collection, and needs no groups when every shard has a model entry.
- `test_qk_clip.py`: a passed group is used with no global read. An omitted group warns and reduces over the same global group. A model without logits needs no group.

On 4 GPUs against its base, 22 of the 23 test files that exercise this change finish. In those 22, no test that passes on the base fails here. Across the 19 files with a pytest summary, 642 tests pass here vs 628 on the base. The 12 tests of the new `test_optimizer_process_groups.py` pass. `test_qk_clip.py` renames one test and adds one: 3 pass here vs 2 on the base. One test in `test_layer_wise_optimizer.py` fails on the base and passes here. The three `generalized_tensor_parallel` test files run no tests on either side; they skip because the container's Transformer Engine is older than GTP needs. `distributed/mfsdp_v2/test_mcore_hybrid.py` timed out on both sides. 78 tests in `dist_checkpointing/test_optimizer.py` fail on both sides because they need 8 ranks; they pass on 8 GPUs (two nodes) in the integration run. The two CUDA-graph end-to-end cases in `distributed/mfsdp_v1/test_mcore_fully_sharded_data_parallel.py` fail on both sides, the same way as on main.

In the integration run, which merges all #6307 PRs onto main 77391e71cc, this PR's test files show no regressions against main on 4 GPUs and 8 GPUs (two nodes). `test_mcore_hybrid.py` timed out there on both sides as well. End-to-end training smokes on that tree (22 configurations on 4 GPUs) give bit-identical losses to main and record no process-group fallback warning. Before the sync, the branch also ran on 4 CPU gloo ranks, one test file at a time, with no regressions. On CPU, 9 tests in the new file pass and 3 need CUDA. The checker tests pass.

**Compatibility.**
- On the standard grid the groups are the same, so checkpoints do not change. The new constructor argument is optional and keyword-only. `GraphedGradCopyFloat16Optimizer` forwards it.
- The rebuild checks its groups at the first checkpoint save that needs a rebuild, not at construction. Such a save needs GTP, distributed Muon and Mamba or GDP `in_proj`. `setup_process_groups_for_optimizer` accepts a collection with neither `dp_cp` nor `dp_cp_gtp_remat` when CP is 1, and the rebuild then raises. The DP×CP group does not change the rebuilt entry, because a GTP shard elects its writer over the group stamped on the parameter.
- Without a collection, the rebuild resolves `dp_cp` along with `tp` and `dp_cp_gtp_remat`. That is one global group more than before, and the standard grid never uses it.
- The rebuild warns under the name `Float16OptimizerWithFloat16Params`, also for `GraphedGradCopyFloat16Optimizer`.
- Not changed here: `LayerWiseDistributedOptimizer` reads `expt_dp` through `getattr(..., None)`. A collection without it treats the expert data-parallel axis as size 1 and passes `None`, which `torch.distributed` reads as WORLD, to the expert all-gather. That predates this PR, and every in-repo collection sets `expt_dp`.
- The test-caller commit touches 19 test files across several CODEOWNERS groups. Should it move into its own PR?
- Needs `determinism-exempt`: `optimizer/__init__.py` and `optimizer/optimizer.py` are registered kernel files. The changes there are group plumbing and warnings; numerics do not change.

Synced with main 77391e71cc on 2026-11-01 by a merge commit that lists each conflict and its resolution, so existing commits and review links stay valid.

+"""``clip_qk`` reduces the maximum attention logits over the group its caller passes."""
+
+import warnings
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest import mock
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core import parallel_state, process_groups_config
+from megatron.core.optimizer.qk_clip import clip_qk
+from megatron.core.process_groups_config import ProcessGroupFallbackWarning
+from tests.unit_tests.test_utilities import Utils, forbid_global_process_groups
+
+
+class _SelfAttention:
+    """The parts of an attention module that ``clip_qk`` touches."""
+
+    def __init__(self, max_attn_logits):
+        self.core_attention = SimpleNamespace(current_max_attn_logits=max_attn_logits)
+        self.clipped_with = None
+
+    def clip_qk(self):
+        self.clipped_with = self.core_attention.current_max_attn_logits.clone()
+
+
+def _model_with_logits(max_attn_logits):
+    """One model chunk, wrapped like the training loop's, with one attention layer."""
+    self_attention = _SelfAttention(max_attn_logits)
+    layer = SimpleNamespace(self_attention=self_attention)
+    decoder = SimpleNamespace(layers=[layer])
+    chunk = SimpleNamespace(module=SimpleNamespace(module=SimpleNamespace(decoder=decoder)))
+    return [chunk], self_attention
+
+
+def _rank_logits():
+    """Per-head maxima that differ on every rank: [rank, -rank]."""
+    rank = torch.distributed.get_rank()
+    return torch.tensor([float(rank), -float(rank)], device='cuda')
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def fresh_warning_registry(monkeypatch):
+    """The test observes the first fallback warning of clip_qk in this process."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(process_groups_config, "_warned_global_process_group_fallbacks", set())
+
+
+class TestClipQKGroup:
+
+    def setup_method(self, method):
+        Utils.initialize_model_parallel()
+
+    def teardown_method(self, method):
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+
+    def test_reduces_over_the_given_group_without_global_reads(self, fresh_warning_registry):
+        world_size = Utils.world_size
+        if world_size % 2 != 0:
+            pytest.skip(f"world size {world_size} must be even to form pairs")
+
+        # The global DP x CP group spans every rank; the model's group pairs neighbours.
+        pair_group, _ = torch.distributed.new_subgroups_by_enumeration(
+            [[r, r + 1] for r in range(0, world_size, 2)]
+        )
+        model, self_attention = _model_with_logits(_rank_logits())
+
+        with forbid_global_process_groups(), warnings.catch_warnings():
+            warnings.simplefilter("error", ProcessGroupFallbackWarning)
+            log_max = clip_qk(model, dp_cp_group=pair_group)
+
+        rank = torch.distributed.get_rank()
+        low, high = rank - rank % 2, rank - rank % 2 + 1
+        expected = torch.tensor([float(high), -float(low)], device='cuda')
+        assert torch.equal(self_attention.clipped_with, expected)
+        assert log_max == float(high)
+
+    def test_without_a_group_warns_and_reduces_over_the_global_dp_cp_group(
+        self, fresh_warning_registry
+    ):
+        model, self_attention = _model_with_logits(_rank_logits())
+
+        with (
+            mock.patch.object(
+                torch.distributed, 'all_reduce', wraps=torch.distributed.all_reduce
+            ) as all_reduce,
+            pytest.warns(
+                ProcessGroupFallbackWarning, match="clip_qk was called without `dp_cp_group`"
+            ),
+        ):
+            log_max = clip_qk(model)
+
+        # The fallback reduces over the global DP x CP group, GTP-remat peers included.
+        global_dp_cp_group = parallel_state.get_data_parallel_group(with_context_parallel=True)
+        assert all_reduce.call_args.kwargs['group'] is global_dp_cp_group
+        world_size = Utils.world_size
+        expected = torch.tensor([float(world_size - 1), 0.0], device='cuda')
+        assert torch.equal(self_attention.clipped_with, expected)
+        assert log_max == float(world_size - 1)
+
+    def test_without_logits_needs_no_group(self, fresh_warning_registry):
+        model, self_attention = _model_with_logits(None)
+
+        with forbid_global_process_groups(), warnings.catch_warnings():
+            warnings.simplefilter("error", ProcessGroupFallbackWarning)
+            log_max = clip_qk(model)
+
+        assert log_max == 0
+        assert self_attention.clipped_with is None

+    # shard, filled here with that shard's 1-based index.

+    num_expert_shards = pg_collection.ep.size() * num_egtp_remat_ranks
+    expert_shard_index = (

+    new_group, _ = torch.distributed.new_subgroups_by_enumeration([list(r) for r in rank_lists])
+    return new_group
+
+
+def build_test_pg_collection(*, tp=1, pp=1, cp=1, ep=1, expt_tp=None, order="tp-cp-ep-dp-pp"):
+    """Build the ProcessGroupCollection of a standard grid without the parallel_state globals.
+
+    The groups have the same ranks as the ones initialize_model_parallel creates for the same
+    sizes and order, with GTP-remat off and one distributed-optimizer instance. In that
+    configuration the GTP-remat and partial data-parallel fields span the same ranks as the plain
+    groups, so they reuse them: dp_gtp_remat, dp_cp_gtp_remat, intra_dp_cp, expt_dp_gtp_remat,
+    intra_expt_dp and tp_ep_pp_with_egtp_remat. The fields it does not build are set to None
+    explicitly, so no resolver falls back to the global grid for an absent field: hcp, gtp_remat,
+    expt_gtp_remat, inter_dist_opt, dp_cp_ag, expt_dp_ag, and the Gloo groups intra_dp_cp_gloo
+    and intra_expt_dp_gloo, as in a job built without Gloo groups. dynamic_cp and dynamic_tp_cp
+    are empty, as they are without dynamic context parallelism.
+
+    Creating groups is collective: call this on every rank, and release the groups with
+    destroy_test_pg_collection.
+
+    Args:
+        tp, pp, cp, ep: Tensor, pipeline, context and expert parallel sizes.
+        expt_tp: Expert tensor parallel size; defaults to `tp`.
+        order: Rank order, as for initialize_model_parallel.
+    """
+    expt_tp = tp if expt_tp is None else expt_tp
+    world_size = torch.distributed.get_world_size()
+    if world_size % (tp * cp * pp) or world_size % (expt_tp * ep * pp):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"world size {world_size} must be divisible by tp*cp*pp ({tp * cp * pp}) "
+            f"and by expt_tp*ep*pp ({expt_tp * ep * pp})"
+        )
+    dims = order.split("-")
+    if sorted(dims) != sorted(["tp", "cp", "ep", "dp", "pp"]):
+        raise ValueError(f"order must arrange tp, cp, ep, dp and pp, got {order!r}")
+    sizes = {
+        "tp": tp,
+        "cp": cp,
+        "dp": world_size // (tp * cp * pp),
+        "pp": pp,
+        "expt_tp": expt_tp,
+        "ep": ep,
+        "expt_dp": world_size // (expt_tp * ep * pp),
+    }
+    # Dense layers have no ep axis and expert layers no cp axis, as in initialize_model_parallel.
+    dense_dims = [dim for dim in dims if dim != "ep"]
+    expert_dims = [{"tp": "expt_tp", "dp": "expt_dp"}.get(dim, dim) for dim in dims if dim != "cp"]
+    grid = HyperCommGrid([sizes[dim] for dim in dense_dims], dense_dims)
+    # The expert layers factor the same ranks differently but share the pipeline groups.
+    grid.register_view(
+        "expert", [sizes[dim] for dim in expert_dims], expert_dims, shared_dims=["pp"]
+    )
+
+    dp = grid.create_pg("dp")
+    dp_cp = grid.create_pg(["cp", "dp"])
+    expt_dp = grid.create_pg("expt_dp", view="expert")
+    tp_ep_pp = grid.create_pg(["expt_tp", "ep", "pp"], view="expert")
+    # Every rank creates every embedding group, in the same order; other ranks get None.
+    pp_rank_lists = grid.get_rank_enum("pp")
+    embd, _ = torch.distributed.new_subgroups_by_enumeration(
+        [ps.default_embedding_ranks(ranks) for ranks in pp_rank_lists]
+    )
+    pos_embd, _ = torch.distributed.new_subgroups_by_enumeration(
+        [ps.default_position_embedding_ranks(ranks) for ranks in pp_rank_lists]
+    )
+    return ProcessGroupCollection(
+        tp=grid.create_pg("tp"),
+        cp=grid.create_pg("cp"),
+        dynamic_cp={},
+        dynamic_tp_cp={},
+        pp=grid.create_pg("pp"),
+        mp=grid.create_pg(["tp", "pp"]),
+        tp_cp=grid.create_pg(["tp", "cp"]),
+        tp_dp_cp=grid.create_pg(["tp", "cp", "dp"]),
+        dp=dp,
+        dp_gtp_remat=dp,
+        dp_cp=dp_cp,
+        dp_cp_gtp_remat=dp_cp,
+        intra_dp_cp=dp_cp,
+        embd=embd,
+        pos_embd=pos_embd,
+        ep=grid.create_pg("ep", view="expert"),
+        expt_tp=grid.create_pg("expt_tp", view="expert"),
+        tp_ep=grid.create_pg(["expt_tp", "ep"], view="expert"),
+        tp_ep_pp=tp_ep_pp,
+        tp_ep_pp_with_egtp_remat=tp_ep_pp,
+        expt_dp=expt_dp,
+        expt_dp_gtp_remat=expt_dp,
+        intra_expt_dp=expt_dp,
+        intra_dp_cp_gloo=None,
+        intra_expt_dp_gloo=None,
+        intra_dist_opt=grid.create_pg(dense_dims),
+        hcp=None,
+        gtp_remat=None,
+        expt_gtp_remat=None,
+        inter_dist_opt=None,
+        dp_cp_ag=None,
+        expt_dp_ag=None,
+    )
+
+
+def destroy_test_pg_collection(pg_collection):
+    """Destroy this rank's groups of a build_test_pg_collection result; call on every rank."""
+    # Every rank finishes its collectives before any communicator goes away.
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    torch.distributed.barrier()
+    groups = {
+        id(group): group
+        for group in vars(pg_collection).values()
+        if isinstance(group, torch.distributed.ProcessGroup)
+    }
+    for group in groups.values():
+        torch.distributed.destroy_process_group(group)
